name: Yeltsin Center
watch: Meduza (Mar 2026) reports average annual donations fell c. 14-fold in 2023–24 versus 2015–22. Its anti-war statement was deleted on police orders; events cancelled under pressure include Nina Khrushcheva's book launch (25 Nov 2024, after a Z-channel denunciation); KPRF bills to close it failed in the Duma.
why_flagged: Meduza (Mar 2026) reports average annual donations fell c. 14-fold in 2023–24 versus 2015–22. Its anti-war statement was deleted on police orders; events cancelled under pressure include Nina Khrushcheva's book launch (25 Nov 2024, after a Z-channel denunciation); KPRF bills to close it failed in the Duma.
records_note: The centre posts yearly accounting statements and names its trustees and board; it has no annual report and its partners page lists no sponsors.

name: King Abdulaziz Center for World Culture (Ithra)
why_flagged: Established, built and run by Saudi Aramco, the national oil company, 82% owned by the Saudi government.
records_note: Ithra posts 2023 and 2024 annual reports; its parent Aramco posts reports for 2019 to 2025 with financials and an 11-member board.
other_findings: WikiLeaks, 2009-10: The Dhahran consulate calls the centre King Abdullah's own project, given to state-owned Aramco, which it calls the King's preferred tool. (Cablegate 09DHAHRAN265)

name: ArtScience Museum
records_note: The museum has no records of its own; owner Marina Bay Sands posts annual reports and parent Las Vegas Sands files 10-Ks with the SEC.

name: Tanoto Art Foundation
watch: RGE (pulp, palm oil) includes Pacific Oil & Gas (unverified claim).
why_flagged: RGE (pulp, palm oil) includes Pacific Oil & Gas (unverified claim).
records_note: The foundation posts no annual report, accounts, donor list or board; its About page names only a curator, a communications manager and an adviser.

name: Gwangju Biennale
watch: The Park Seo-Bo Prize was abolished in 2023 after one edition, following public protest.
why_flagged: Public funding and related spending top 10 billion won per edition; the 2026 operating budget is about 14.3 billion won. Park Seo-Bo's GIZI Foundation funded a prize until 2023.
records_note: The foundation lists its trustees and auditors by name, posts audited financial statements (2020 and 2021 seen), and shows past sponsors as logos.
other_findings: WikiLeaks, 2007-09: KBS journalists told the embassy the Shin Jeong-ah scandal showed a senior presidential aide pressing a university to hire her. Shin had just been named co-director of the 2008 Biennale. (Cablegate 07SEOUL2876)

name: Arter
watch: Koç Holding owns Tüpraş (oil refining) and Otokar (military vehicles).
why_flagged: Koç Holding owns Tüpraş (oil refining) and Otokar (military vehicles).
records_note: Arter has none of its own; parent Vehbi Koç Foundation posts reports for 2012 to 2025 without audited accounts. Arter names sponsors, lists its board.

name: Art-Siadziba
watch: Founded 24 Dec 2011 by Stas Babaitsau, Franak Viačorka, Zmicier Afanasenka and Pavel Belavus to promote Belarusian-language culture among the young; moved repeatedly after evictions (Horizont club, Pushkin Ave 28a, an underground flat, Instrumentalnaya 6 from Oct 2013). Map point is approximate, near the last premises.
records_note: Liquidated on 23 July 2021; its site artsiadziba.by returned no content, so reports, accounts, funders and board were not checked.

name: Belarusian State Museum of the History of the Great Patriotic War
watch: Belarus's most-visited museum, in the 2014 'Victory' building at Praspiekt Pieramožcaŭ 8 (4,200 m2, 10 halls, 8,000+ exhibits shown). Official records cite Belstat for 196,700 visitors in 2020 (Covid year) and also carries an unsourced 'about 570,000 a year' line; the museum's own site says only 'hundreds of thousands'. Sized S on the verifiable figure; could be L if the pre-Covid claim holds.
records_note: A state museum under the Ministry of Culture; its site posts no annual reports, accounts or sponsors, and lists only administrators, not a board.

name: National Centre for Contemporary Arts
watch: State body formed 1 Oct 2015 by merging the Museum of Modern Fine Arts (1997) with the Creative Workshops centre; c.4,936 works; venues at Nekrasova 3 and Independence Ave 47. Director Siarhei Kryshtapovich (since 2018) was commissioner of Belarus's last official Venice pavilion, 'Exit' (2019), organised with the Culture Ministry and the embassy in Italy. Its sites (ncsm.by, artmodern.museum.by) show no partners page. The current and previous culture ministers were not found on sanctions lists in the pages opened.
records_note: A state-budget body being liquidated under a 3 August 2026 resolution; its site no longer resolves and the ministry posts no accounts for it.

name: Official. Unofficial. Belarus (Belarus at the Venice Biennale, 2026 collateral event)
watch: 9 May–22 Nov 2026 at the church of San Giovanni Evangelista, San Polo 2454, an official collateral event of the 61st Biennale, curated by Daniella and Natalia Kaliada with Tsesler, Padhaiskaya, Hrynevich, Khalezin and chef Rasmus Munk; audio by Gillian Anderson, Stephen Fry, Jude Law and others. The state pavilion (Culture Ministry + NCCA, commissioner Kryshtapovich; last shown 2019, 'Exit') was absent in 2022 and 2024, so this is the first Belarusian presence since 2019 and it is unofficial.
records_note: A one-off Venice event run by Belarus Free Theatre, so the theatre's Companies House accounts and trustee list apply; no funder is named.

name: Tokyo Arts and Space
funding: Its 2026 shows are run and paid for by the Tokyo Metropolitan Foundation for History and Culture (Tokyo government). The Korean Embassy and Cultural Center back one show.
watch: As Tokyo Wonder Site (2006-07), it was at the centre of a nepotism row over Governor Ishihara's son's paid role, raised in the Tokyo assembly.
records_note: Its operator, the Tokyo history and culture foundation, posts reports for FY2017 to FY2025, accounts for FY2020 to FY2025, a board list and named donors.

name: AZ Museum (Anatoly Zverev Museum)
watch: Opened 2015; half the collection donated by Aliki Costakis. OpenSanctions shows Opaleva only as a Russian company-register record, not sanctioned.
records_note: This private museum's site has no annual reports, accounts, funder list or board; press says its founder funds it from her own money.
